metadata.title: Decoding by Linear Programming

nodes.name: Error Correcting Decoding Problem
nodes.statement: Recover an input vector $f \in \mathbb{R}^n$ from corrupted measurements $y = Af + e$, where $A$ is an $m \times n$ coding matrix ($m > n$) and $e$ is an arbitrary unknown error vector.

nodes.name: Sparsest Solution ($P_0$)
nodes.statement: $(P_0)\quad \min_{d \in \mathbb{R}^m} \|d\|_{\ell_0} \text{ subject to } Fd = \tilde{y}\,(=Fe)$. Finding the sparsest solution to an underdetermined system of linear equations.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit ($P_1$)
nodes.statement: $(P_1)\quad \min_{d \in \mathbb{R}^m} \|d\|_{\ell_1}, \; Fd = \tilde{y}$. Convex $\ell_1$ relaxation of $(P_0)$, recastable as a linear program.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ Decoding ($P_1'$)
nodes.statement: $(P_1')\quad \min_{g \in \mathbb{R}^n} \|y - Ag\|_{\ell_1}$. Direct $\ell_1$ decoding formulation; equivalent to $(P_1)$ via $g = f + h$, $x = e - Ah$.

nodes.name: Sparse-error assumption
nodes.statement: $\|e\|_{\ell_0} := |\{i : e_i \neq 0\}| \leq \rho \cdot m$ for some $\rho > 0$.

nodes.name: Annihilator reduction
nodes.statement: Choose $F$ with $FA = 0$; then $\tilde{y} = F(Af + e) = Fe$, reducing decoding to recovering sparse $e$ from $Fe$.

nodes.name: LP reformulation of $(P_1')$
nodes.statement: $\min 1^T t,\; -t \leq y - Ag \leq t$, with variables $t \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $g \in \mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Restricted Isometry Constants $\delta_S$
nodes.statement: For $1 \leq S \leq |J|$, $\delta_S$ is the smallest quantity such that $(1-\delta_S)\|c\|^2 \leq \|F_T c\|^2 \leq (1+\delta_S)\|c\|^2$ for every $T \subset J$ with $|T| \leq S$ and all real coefficients $(c_j)_{j \in T}$.

nodes.name: Restricted Orthogonality Constants $\theta_{S,S'}$
nodes.statement: For $S + S' \leq |J|$, $\theta_{S,S'}$ is the smallest quantity such that $|\langle F_T c, F_{T'} c'\rangle| \leq \theta_{S,S'} \cdot \|c\|\,\|c'\|$ for all disjoint $T, T' \subseteq J$ with $|T| \leq S$ and $|T'| \leq S'$.

nodes.name: Compressible signal class $\mathcal{F}_s(B)$
nodes.statement: Class of $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^m$ whose decreasing rearrangement obeys $|\alpha|_{(k)} \leq B \cdot k^{-s}$ for some $s \geq 1$.

nodes.name: Uniform Uncertainty Principle (UUP)
nodes.statement: A random matrix $F$ obeys the UUP with oversampling factor $\lambda$ if $\delta_S \leq 1/2$ for $S = \rho \cdot K/\lambda$ with probability at least $1 - O(N^{-\gamma/\rho})$.

nodes.name: Exact Reconstruction Principle (ERP)
nodes.statement: $F$ obeys ERP with oversampling factor $\lambda$ if for each $T$ with $|T| \leq S$ and each sign vector $c$ on $T$, there exists w.h.p. a vector $w$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle = c_j$ for $j \in T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| \leq 1/2$ for $j \notin T$.

nodes.name: Relation between $\theta$ and $\delta$
nodes.statement: $\theta_{S,S'} \leq \delta_{S+S'} \leq \theta_{S,S'} + \max(\delta_S, \delta_{S'})$ for all $S, S'$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness from $\delta_{2S} < 1$
nodes.statement: If $\delta_{2S} < 1$ and $|T| \leq S$, then $T$ and $(c_j)_{j \in T}$ can be uniquely reconstructed from $f := F_T c$ and the $v_j$'s.
conclusions: Pair $(T, (c_j)_{j \in T})$ is uniquely determined by $f$ and $\{v_j\}$

nodes.name: Dual sparse reconstruction property, $\ell_2$ version
nodes.statement: If $\delta_S < 1$ and $c$ is supported on $T$ with $|T| \leq S$, there exists $w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle_H = c_j$ for $j \in T$, an exceptional set $E$ disjoint from $T$ with $|E| \leq S'$, $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| \leq \theta_{S,S'}/((1-\delta_S)\sqrt{S'}) \cdot \|c\|$ for $j \notin T \cup E$, and $(\sum_{j \in E} |\langle w, v_j\rangle|^2)^{1/2} \leq \theta_S/(1-\delta_S) \cdot \|c\|$.
conclusions: Existence of $w$ matching $c$ on $T$ with controlled $\ell_2$ tail outside $T \cup E$

nodes.name: Dual sparse reconstruction property, $\ell_\infty$ version
nodes.statement: If $\delta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ and $c$ is supported on $T$ with $|T| \leq S$, there exists $w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle = c_j$ on $T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| \leq \theta_S / ((1-\delta_S - \theta_{S,2S})\sqrt{S}) \cdot \|c\|$ for all $j \notin T$.
conclusions: Existence of dual vector $w$ with uniform $\ell_\infty$ control off $T$

nodes.name: Restricted isometry tail bound for Gaussian $F$
nodes.statement: Let $r = S/m$ and $f(r) := \sqrt{m/p}\,(\sqrt{r} + \sqrt{2H(r)})$ with $H(q) = -q\log q - (1-q)\log(1-q)$. For each $\epsilon > 0$, $P(1 + \delta_S > [1 + (1+\epsilon)f(r)]^2) \leq 2 e^{-mH(r)\epsilon/2}$.
assumptions: $F$ is $p \times m$ Gaussian with i.i.d. entries, mean 0, variance $1/p$

nodes.name: Main $\ell_1$ Recovery Theorem
nodes.statement: If $S \geq 1$ satisfies $\delta_S + \theta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$, and $c$ is a real vector supported on $T \subset J$ with $|T| \leq S$, then $c$ is the unique minimizer of $(P_1)\;\min \|d\|_{\ell_1},\; Fd = f$ where $f := Fc$.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ Decoding Recovery Theorem
nodes.statement: Suppose $F$ satisfies $FA = 0$ and $S \geq 1$ obeys the hypothesis of Theorem 1.4. Set $y = Af + e$ with $e$ supported on a set of size at most $S$. Then $f$ is the unique minimizer of $(P_1')\;\min_g \|y - Ag\|_{\ell_1}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian Restricted Isometry Theorem
nodes.statement: If $F$ is $p \times m$ Gaussian with i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0,1/p)$ entries and $r = S/m < r^*(p,m)$, then the hypothesis of Theorem 1.4 holds with overwhelming probability (decaying exponentially in $m$). Numerically: $r \leq 3.6\cdot 10^{-4}$ for $p/m = 3/4$, $r \leq 3.2\cdot 10^{-4}$ for $p/m = 2/3$, $r \leq 2.3\cdot 10^{-4}$ for $p/m = 1/2$.
assumptions: $F$ is $p \times m$ Gaussian, i.i.d. entries with mean 0, variance $1/p$

nodes.name: Compressible Signal Reconstruction
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be the measurement matrix and $\alpha^\sharp$ the solution to $\min_{\tilde\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^m} \|\tilde\alpha\|_{\ell_1}$ s.t. $F\tilde\alpha = y$. If $S \leq K$ satisfies $\delta_S + 2\theta_S + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ and $\lambda = K/S$, then $\sup_{\alpha \in \mathcal{F}_s(B)} \|\alpha - \alpha^\sharp\| \leq C \cdot (K/\lambda)^{-(s-1/2)}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian Coding Matrix Decoding
nodes.statement: If $A$ is $n \times m$ Gaussian and $p = m - n$, then under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.6, the solution to $(P_1')$ is unique and equal to $f$.
conclusions: The minimizer of $(P_1')$ is unique and equals $f$

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur / Geman-Silverstein extremal eigenvalue limits
nodes.statement: For a $p \times m$ matrix $F$ with i.i.d. Gaussian entries of variance $1/p$ and a fixed $T$ with $|T|/p \to \gamma \leq 1$ as $p, |T| \to \infty$: $\lambda_{\min}(F_T^* F_T) \to (1 - \sqrt{\gamma})^2$ a.s. and $\lambda_{\max}(F_T^* F_T) \to (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$ a.s.
assumptions: $F$ is $p \times m$ Gaussian, i.i.d. entries, variance $1/p$

nodes.name: Ledoux concentration bounds for singular values
nodes.statement: For each fixed $t > 0$: $P(\sigma_{\max}(F_T) > 1 + \sqrt{|T|/p} + o(1) + t) \leq e^{-pt^2/2}$ and $P(\sigma_{\min}(F_T) < 1 - \sqrt{|T|/p} + o(1) - t) \leq e^{-pt^2/2}$.
conclusions: Both deviation probabilities are bounded by $e^{-pt^2/2}$

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ Decoder via Linear Programming
nodes.statement: Solve $(P_1')\;\min_g \|y - Ag\|_{\ell_1}$, recast as the LP $\min 1^T t,\; -t \leq y - Ag \leq t$, to recover $f$ from corrupted measurements $y = Af + e$.

nodes.name: Iterative Dual Vector Construction
nodes.statement: Construct the dual certificate $w$ for Lemma 2.2 by iteratively applying Lemma 2.1: at each step, build $w_{n+1}$ that annihilates $w_n$ on the previous exceptional set $T_n$, then form $w := \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n-1} w_n$.
input: Sign pattern $c$ supported on $T$ with $|T| \leq S$
output: Dual vector $w \in H$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle = c_j$ on $T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle|$ small off $T$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.2 (approximate orthogonality)
nodes.statement: By homogeneity, reduce to unit-norm case; apply the parallelogram identity $\langle f, g\rangle = (\|f+g\|^2 - \|f-g\|^2)/4$ together with the restricted isometry inequalities to bound the inner product.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.3 (uniqueness)
nodes.statement: Suppose $f$ has two distinct sparse representations; then $F_{T \cup T'} d = 0$ for some nonzero $d$ with $|T \cup T'| \leq 2S$, contradicting $\delta_{2S} < 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Set $w := F_T (F_T^* F_T)^{-1} c_T$ using invertibility from $\delta_S < 1$; bound $\|F_{T'}^* w\|$ via duality and (1.8); the exceptional set $E$ where $|\langle w, v_j\rangle|$ is large must have size at most $S'$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Iteratively apply Lemma 2.1 to obtain $w_n$ that annihilates $w_{n-1}$ on the exceptional set; sum the alternating series $w := \sum (-1)^{n-1} w_n$ which converges by the contraction $\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S) \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4
nodes.statement: By duality, exhibit $w$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle = \mathrm{sgn}(c_j)$ on $T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| < 1$ off $T$ (Lemma 2.2). Compare $\|d\|_{\ell_1}$ to $\|c\|_{\ell_1}$ via this dual vector to force $d = c$ on $T$ and $d = 0$ off $T$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Apply the Ledoux concentration bound to a fixed $T$, then take a union bound over all $\binom{m}{S}$ subsets using Stirling's $\log\binom{m}{S} = mH(r) + O(\log m)$.

nodes.name: Set up dual certificate $w$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.2 (with the additional $\theta_S$ term in the hypothesis), there exists $w$ with $\langle w, v_j\rangle_H = \mathrm{sgn}(c_j)$ on $T$ and $|\langle w, v_j\rangle_H| < 1$ for $j \notin T$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\|d\|_{\ell_1}$ using $w$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\|d\|_{\ell_1} = \sum_{j \in T} |c_j + (d_j - c_j)| + \sum_{j \notin T} |d_j|$ and bound below by $\sum_T \mathrm{sgn}(c_j)(c_j + (d_j - c_j)) + \sum_{j \notin T} d_j \langle w, v_j\rangle$.

nodes.name: Apply $Fd = Fc = f$
nodes.statement: Use $\sum_{j \in J} d_j v_j = \sum_{j \in T} c_j v_j = f$ to show the lower bound equals $\sum_{j \in T} |c_j| = \|c\|_{\ell_1}$.

nodes.name: Force equality and conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\|d\|_{\ell_1} \leq \|c\|_{\ell_1}$ also holds (as $c$ is feasible), all inequalities are equalities; strict $|\langle w, v_j\rangle| < 1$ off $T$ forces $d_j = 0$ for $j \notin T$, then $\delta_S < 1$ gives $d_j = c_j$ on $T$.

nodes.name: Initialize: apply Lemma 2.1 to obtain $w_1$
nodes.statement: Normalize $\sum_{j \in T} |c_j|^2 = S$. Use Lemma 2.1 with $T_0 = T$ to get $w_1 \in H$ and $T_1 \subseteq J \setminus T_0$, $|T_1| \leq S$, matching $c$ on $T_0$.

nodes.name: Iterative annihilation step
nodes.statement: For $n \geq 1$ apply Lemma 2.1 with input supported on $T_n$ to get $w_{n+1}$ that annihilates $w_n$ on $T_n$ and is zero on $T_0$, with $|\langle w_{n+1}, v_j\rangle| \leq (\theta_S/(1-\delta_S))(\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S))^n$ off $T_0 \cup T_n \cup T_{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Sum the alternating series
nodes.statement: Define $w := \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n-1} w_n$; series converges absolutely because $\theta_{S,2S}/(1-\delta_S) < 1$ by hypothesis.

nodes.name: Cancellation and $\ell_\infty$ bound off $T_0$
nodes.statement: For $j \in T_0$, only $w_1$ contributes giving $\langle w, v_j\rangle = c_j$. For $j \notin T_0$, consecutive terms with $j \in T_n$ and $j \in T_{n+1}$ cancel; remaining terms sum geometrically to $\theta_{S,S}/(1-\delta_S - \theta_{S,2S})$.

nodes.name: Bound a single $\lambda_{\max}$ deviation
nodes.statement: For fixed $T$ with $|T| = S$, apply Ledoux's bound: $P(\lambda_{\max}(F_T^* F_T) > (1 + \sqrt{S/p} + \eta_p + t)^2) \leq e^{-pt^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Union bound via Stirling
nodes.statement: Use $\log\binom{m}{S} = mH(r) + O(\log m)$ with $r = S/m$ to bound $P(\sup_{|T|=S} \lambda_{\max} > \cdots) \leq e^{mH(r)} e^{O(\log m)} e^{-pt^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Choose $t$ and absorb error terms
nodes.statement: Set $\eta_p + t = (1+\epsilon)\sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)}$, assume $m, p$ large enough so $\eta_p \leq (\epsilon/2)\sqrt{m/p}\sqrt{2H(r)}$; resulting bound is $\leq e^{-mH(r)\epsilon/2}$. Same bound for $\lambda_{\min}$.

nodes.name: Numerical experiment, $m = 2n$
nodes.statement: For $A$ an $m \times n$ Gaussian matrix with $m = 2n$ and $m \in \{512, 1024\}$: 100 trials per error fraction. $\ell_1$ recovery succeeds with frequency 1 as long as the fraction of corrupted entries is below about 17%.

nodes.name: Numerical experiment, $m = 4n$
nodes.statement: For $A$ an $m \times n$ Gaussian matrix with $m = 4n$ and $m = 512$ ($n = 128$): $\ell_1$ recovery succeeds with frequency 1 as long as the fraction of corrupted entries is below about 34%.

nodes.name: Half-corruption impossibility
nodes.statement: For $m = 2n$, choose two distinct plaintexts $f, f'$; form $g \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with half its coefficients from $Af$ and half from $Af'$. Then $g = Af + e = Af' + e'$ with $|\mathrm{supp}(e)|, |\mathrm{supp}(e')| \leq m/2$, so decoding is impossible when error support has size $\geq m/2$.

nodes.name: Improvability of dual construction
nodes.statement: The condition $\delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} < 1$ might be relaxed by designing each $w_n$ to merely moderate (rather than annihilate) the influence of $w_{n-1}$ on $T_{n-1}$, at the cost of substantially more complex calculations.

nodes.name: Lower limit of the present approach
nodes.statement: $\liminf_{S \to \infty,\,S/m \to r} \delta_S + \theta_{S,S} + \theta_{S,2S} \geq J(m/p \cdot r)$ where $J(r) := 2\sqrt{r} + r + (2 + \sqrt{2})\sqrt{r(1-r)} + \sqrt{r(1-2r)}$. $J(r) > 1$ iff $r > 2.36 \cdot 10^{-2}$, so improving Theorem 1.6 beyond about 2% requires new ideas.

nodes.name: Alternative coding matrices
nodes.statement: Partial Fourier matrices and noiselets (Coifman-Geshwind-Meyer) likely also yield exact $\ell_1$ decoding and admit fast algorithms for applying $A$ or $A^*$.

nodes.name: Compressible Signal Recovery
nodes.statement: Reconstruct an object $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}_s(B)$ from $K \ll m$ linear measurements $y = F\alpha$ via $\min \|\tilde\alpha\|_{\ell_1}$ s.t. $F\tilde\alpha = y$.
